_about: Shared cases for the sensitivity-declaration parity check. This file is the ONE
source of cases for both readers of a sensitivity declaration: the compiler's
reader over a compiled schema, and this plugin's reader over the authored entity
JSON it receives. Both sides enumerate this file, so a case added here is checked
on both sides and a case removed from here fails the compiler-side check's
shape-class census. Add a case HERE rather than inline in either reader's own
unit tests, or the two sides stop being compared on it.
Every `schema` value is an entity's authored spec.schema, written in JSON because
that is the form the plugin receives (the host converts the entity YAML to JSON
before invoking a rule) and because JSON is valid YAML, so the compiler side
compiles the identical bytes.
`expect` is the compiler-side truth: the flat-dotted leaf paths, per pillar, that
the compiler reads as declared sensitive. An omitted pillar means the empty set.
`guestBlindPaths` names paths the plugin-side reader cannot reach because the
declaration is nested inside a YAML text block that only a YAML parser can open.
The plugin has no YAML parser, so the divergence is real and is recorded here
rather than hidden: the plugin side asserts it collects `expect` MINUS these, and
that it reports exactly these as unreadable.
`pillarKeyCases` is the second question this file holds: which property names one
pillar of an authored spec.schema EXPOSES. The compiler answers it by compiling
the pillar and reading the property map the compilation produces; the plugin
answers it by classifying the pillar's own authored node. `expectKeys` is the
compiler-side truth, measured from the compiler's own reader.
`guestReadable` records which side of one line each case sits on. A pillar node
that is a reference is read through the definition it points at, with any
property map written beside the reference read too, when the pointer resolves
inside the pillar node — the document the compiler compiles that pillar as. A
reference resolving nowhere inside it, a composition, and an escaped body
authored as YAML text are shapes the plugin cannot enumerate: the first names a
target the plugin cannot see, a composition carries its properties inside its
branches, and a text body needs a YAML parser this crate does not have. For
those the plugin reports UNKNOWN rather than a key set, which is why the
divergence is recorded here rather than hidden. Every other case is a shape both
readers must agree on exactly.

leafCases.name: typeless-leaf-declares
leafCases.why: A leaf carrying only the marker is a leaf, not an object with a property named sensitive.

leafCases.name: typed-leaf-declares
leafCases.why: The ordinary shape: a marker beside a type.

leafCases.name: sibling-declares-nothing
leafCases.why: A marker on one leaf must not spread to its siblings.

leafCases.name: pillars-are-independent
leafCases.why: A path is unique only within its pillar, so the same name may differ across pillars.

leafCases.name: nested-implicit-object
leafCases.why: Nesting expressed by YAML hierarchy alone; the collected path is the dotted chain.

leafCases.name: nested-explicit-properties
leafCases.why: Nesting expressed with an authored properties map; `properties` is a keyword, not a leaf name.

leafCases.name: marker-beside-ref
leafCases.why: A marker beside a reference is carried onto the referring node.

leafCases.name: marker-beside-allof
leafCases.why: A marker beside a composition keyword is carried onto the composing node.

leafCases.name: marker-beside-anyof
leafCases.why: Same as allOf; each composition keyword takes the same path.

leafCases.name: marker-beside-oneof
leafCases.why: Same as allOf; each composition keyword takes the same path.

leafCases.name: composition-branch-leaf-declares-on-the-composing-node
leafCases.why: A branch composes onto the object carrying it, so a marker on the branch itself declares the carrying property.

leafCases.name: composition-branch-properties-declare-below-the-composing-node
leafCases.why: A branch's own property map contributes below the carrying property's path, never below the branch.

leafCases.name: conditional-branch-properties-declare-below-the-carrying-node
leafCases.why: The single-schema composition keywords compose the same way as the list-valued ones, so a marker under one of them declares too.

leafCases.name: negated-branch-leaf-declares-on-the-carrying-node
leafCases.why: A negated branch describes a shape an instance must avoid, so reading a marker there can only withhold a datum that could never validate.

leafCases.name: reference-target-declares-at-the-referring-path
leafCases.why: A definitions block authored beside the properties that use it resolves there, and the declaration lands at the referring property's path plus its own chain — no authored datum lives inside the definition.

leafCases.name: reference-target-at-the-document-root-resolves-too
leafCases.why: A definitions block authored at the document root is a reference scope as well, so the same pointer resolves from an outer scope.

leafCases.name: recursive-reference-declaring-terminates-and-withholds-the-tail
leafCases.why: A target that reaches itself cannot be enumerated further, so the referring path is collected when the recursion carries a declaration anywhere.

leafCases.name: recursive-reference-declaring-nothing-stays-readable
leafCases.why: A path is sensitive only when an author said so, so a recursive schema carrying no marker must not be withheld by the cycle rule alone.

leafCases.name: unresolvable-reference-collects-the-referring-path
leafCases.why: What an unresolvable target declares is unknown, so naming the referring property is the most precise declaration available and the only one that cannot under-report. The property map beside the reference is read as declared properties, so its marked leaf is collected below the referring path as well.

leafCases.name: properties-beside-a-reference-declare-below-the-referring-node
leafCases.why: Keys written beside a reference are compact form, read as they would be on the same node without it, so a property map beside a reference that resolves declares below the referring path.

leafCases.name: composition-sibling-properties-are-not-walked
leafCases.why: A property map beside a composition keyword yields no reachable leaf on either side.

leafCases.name: array-items-are-not-walked
leafCases.why: A marker on an array's element type is not a leaf of the enclosing object.

leafCases.name: object-marker-and-nested-marker
leafCases.why: An object may declare the marker itself and still carry declaring children.

leafCases.name: only-boolean-true-declares
leafCases.why: A composed schema records which entity declared a keyword under the same keyword spelling, mapped to an entity name; a presence-only read would take that for a declaration.

leafCases.name: explicit-jsonschema-mode-declares-nothing
leafCases.why: Under an explicit JSON Schema mode the key is authored JSON Schema content, not the compact-form marker.

leafCases.name: escape-mapping-body-declares-at-its-own-node
leafCases.why: Every mapping inside an escaped body is a keyword node, and a compact-form keyword written there keeps its compact-form meaning, so a marker on the body's own node declares the node carrying the escape.

leafCases.name: escape-mapping-body-nested-leaf-declares
leafCases.why: A property map inside an escaped body is read as one, so a marked leaf in it declares below the node carrying the escape.

leafCases.name: escape-mapping-body-reads-properties-beside-a-composition
leafCases.why: Inside an escaped body nothing is classified by its shape: a property map beside a composition keyword is the node's own property map, where the same spelling outside an escape is not walked.

leafCases.name: escape-mapping-body-marker-beside-a-reference-declares
leafCases.why: A reference inside an escaped body is a keyword node like any other, so a marker beside it declares the node carrying the escape.

leafCases.name: reference-target-inside-an-escape-body-is-read-as-json-schema
leafCases.why: A definition authored inside an escaped body is read the way the body is, so a property map beside a composition in that definition is walked when a reference reaches it.

leafCases.name: escape-text-body-is-unreadable-in-the-guest
leafCases.why: A YAML text block needs a YAML parser to open; the guest has none, so this divergence is declared rather than hidden.

leafCases.name: pillar-node-reference-declares-through-its-target
leafCases.why: A pillar whose own node is a reference is read through the definition it points at, so a marked leaf there is collected at its own path below the pillar and an unmarked sibling is not.

leafCases.name: pillar-node-reference-at-the-document-root-resolves-too
leafCases.why: The document root is a reference scope for a pillar node as it is for a property, so the same pointer resolves from the outer scope.

leafCases.name: pillar-node-reference-beside-properties-declares-from-both
leafCases.why: A reference on the pillar node composes with a property map written beside it, so a declaration in either is collected.

leafCases.name: pillar-node-reference-chain-is-followed
leafCases.why: A target that is itself a reference is followed in turn, and its own property map declares as well.

leafCases.name: pillar-node-unresolvable-reference-adds-nothing
leafCases.why: A pillar has no path of its own to collect in place of a target nobody can find, so the property map beside the pointer is all that declares.

leafCases.name: pillar-node-self-reference-terminates
leafCases.why: A pointer naming the pillar node itself revisits it, which ends the walk rather than recursing.

leafCases.name: pillar-node-reference-marker-on-the-pillar-declares-nothing
leafCases.why: No single datum sits at a pillar node, so a marker written there beside the reference declares nothing on either side.

leafCases.name: pillar-root-as-a-leaf-declares-nothing
leafCases.why: A pillar whose own node reads as a leaf exposes no properties, so nothing is collected — the shape an author hits when naming a property `sensitive`.

leafCases.name: nothing-declared
leafCases.why: The silent half: a schema with no marker anywhere collects nothing.

leafCases.name: pillar-outside-the-axis
leafCases.why: The axis covers values, infra and provides only.

leafCases.name: empty-schema
leafCases.why: An entity with no schema content declares nothing.

slotCases.name: slot-marker-quoted-string
slotCases.why: A non-boolean is not a declaration on either side; the compiler additionally refuses to decode it.

slotCases.name: slot-marker-number
slotCases.why: As above: the marker is boolean-only.

pillarKeyCases.name: pillar-exposes-its-implicit-properties
pillarKeyCases.why: The ordinary shape: every key of the pillar's object scope is a published key.

pillarKeyCases.name: no-provides-pillar-is-an-empty-contract
pillarKeyCases.why: An entity that declares no provides pillar declares no output contract. Empty is an answer, not an absence of one.

pillarKeyCases.name: empty-provides-pillar-is-an-empty-contract
pillarKeyCases.why: As above, written explicitly.

pillarKeyCases.name: pillar-that-is-not-a-mapping-declares-nothing
pillarKeyCases.why: A scalar where an object scope belongs exposes no property on either side.

pillarKeyCases.name: pillar-property-named-like-a-compact-keyword-makes-the-pillar-a-leaf
pillarKeyCases.why: A pillar whose only key is a compact-form keyword classifies as a constraint leaf rather than an object scope, so it exposes nothing. This is the case a naive reader gets wrong in the direction of over-reporting.

pillarKeyCases.name: pillar-with-explicit-properties-exposes-them
pillarKeyCases.why: A structural JSON Schema keyword steers the pillar to the authored-JSON-Schema reading, where the property map is explicit.

pillarKeyCases.name: pillar-declaring-jsonschema-mode-exposes-its-properties
pillarKeyCases.why: An explicit mode overrides the content-shape heuristic on both sides.

pillarKeyCases.name: pillar-declaring-compact-mode-becomes-a-leaf
pillarKeyCases.why: The opposite mode on the same content: a leaf exposes no property map, so the authored keys are not published keys.

pillarKeyCases.name: definitions-blocks-are-reference-scopes-not-properties
pillarKeyCases.why: A definitions block sitting on the pillar names reference targets rather than data, so it contributes no published key.

pillarKeyCases.name: legacy-definitions-block-is-also-a-reference-scope
pillarKeyCases.why: The older spelling of the same block, which a reader excluding only one of the two would get wrong.

pillarKeyCases.name: a-nested-property-adds-no-top-level-key
pillarKeyCases.why: Only the pillar's own level is a published key. A property below one is reached by a dotted path, not by an inject from: reference.

pillarKeyCases.name: escaped-mapping-body-exposes-its-properties
pillarKeyCases.why: An escaped body authored as a mapping replaces the node it sits on and is authored JSON Schema both readers can open.

pillarKeyCases.name: escaped-text-body-is-unreadable-in-the-guest
pillarKeyCases.why: The same body authored as YAML text. The compiler parses it and reads the contract; the plugin has no YAML parser and reports unknown.

provides.$jsonschema:
type: object
properties:
  endpoint:
    type: string

pillarKeyCases.name: reference-pillar-exposes-its-target-properties
pillarKeyCases.why: A pillar that is a bare reference to a definition authored on the pillar node. The contract is the definition's, so its property names are the published keys on both sides.

pillarKeyCases.name: reference-pillar-with-sibling-properties-exposes-both
pillarKeyCases.why: A reference carrying a sibling property map. The reference target and the sibling map both shape the contract, so the published keys are the names of both.

pillarKeyCases.name: reference-pillar-chain-exposes-every-target
pillarKeyCases.why: A target that is itself a reference is followed in turn, nearest definitions block first, and every property map along the chain contributes its names.

pillarKeyCases.name: self-referencing-pillar-terminates
pillarKeyCases.why: A pointer naming the pillar node itself revisits it, which ends the chain; the names are the pillar's own.

pillarKeyCases.name: reference-pillar-pointing-outside-the-pillar-is-unreadable-in-the-guest
pillarKeyCases.why: The compiler compiles a pillar as its own document, so a pointer resolving only against a definitions block beside the pillars finds nothing there and the pillar exposes no name; the plugin cannot see what the pointer names and reports unknown rather than guessing empty.

pillarKeyCases.name: reference-pillar-to-a-composition-is-unreadable-in-the-guest
pillarKeyCases.why: A reference whose target is a composition. Neither reader enters a pillar's contract through a branch, so the compiler exposes no name; the branches carry properties, so the plugin reports unknown as it does for a composition on the pillar node.

pillarKeyCases.name: escaped-body-with-a-composition-is-unreadable-in-the-guest
pillarKeyCases.why: A composition inside an escaped body is read as one keyword beside the body's own property map, so the compiler exposes that map alone; the branches carry properties too, so the plugin reports unknown here as it does for a composition on the pillar node.

pillarKeyCases.name: all-of-pillar-is-unreadable-in-the-guest
pillarKeyCases.why: A composition on the pillar node itself. Its branches carry the properties, and neither reader enters a pillar through a branch.

pillarKeyCases.name: any-of-pillar-is-unreadable-in-the-guest
pillarKeyCases.why: The same shape under the second list-valued composition keyword, because the three are a set and a reader can handle one and miss another.

pillarKeyCases.name: one-of-pillar-is-unreadable-in-the-guest
pillarKeyCases.why: And the third.
